questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore a new city, with a culture different from my own. It was important to me that the city was walkable and student-friendly. Bologna is a great choice in that regard.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I could always just e-mail someone, and they were very chill in Italy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: e-mails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was alright, but i had to reach out for answers a few times. But the procedure was pretty simple when i was there.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had a friend who had some friends living in Bologna the year before us. They gave us a contact for a man named Leif/Laif(?) who helped us find a really great appartment. I recommend living in the south east of Bologna.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: All of Bologna is basically a student-city, so it is no problem to live off campus. For transport etc. i would recommend trying to find something within the city walls.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a great experience personally - but some of my friends had a harder time.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pretty easy - i had to check in via a zoom-meeting. They sent me the link on e-mail. There were only some problems becasue there were some times where you could not check in, but we made it work.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online check in via zoom-meeting.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a person on the zoom-call who told me what to do.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fine. i had originally chosen 4 classes, and i ended up change 3 of them so my schedule made more sense. i had the learning agreement updated when i was there.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take it easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was great! although some of the teachers didnt use powerpoint presentations and spoke either fast, or with a heavy accent so at times it was hard to catch what they were saying.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was fine. I think they are nicer to exchange students at exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH there is always a poerpoint and the teacher makes sure the important points are made in an understandable matter. In Bologna sometimes it was hard to follow, because it went fast and there was a language barrier.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Sports law, Foundations of Private Law, Labour Law, EU Health Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports Law and Labour law was easy peasy. Foundations of Private Law and EU Health law were more challenging, but also interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Lots of travel! Would highly recommend going around and seeing other places as well - trains are pretty cheap sometimes.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: We had to get a fan for the apartment because it was so hot in the summer.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many fun things to do! We played a lot of paddel or hung out in the park.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of history and museums in Bologna.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Florence, Venice, Rimini beach, there is also a lake pretty close to bologna is you take the train to Mazzarboto. We rented a car and went to the dolomites as well - Amazing experience!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. We went to the law introduction day and met our friendgroup for the rest of the trip.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If there is an introduction day - go to it, and then ask the people close to you if you should get a coffee afterwards.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The locals are more calm, and less focused on optimizing than scandinavians. I often found myself walking behind a group of really slow walking locals who did not seem to notice or care that someone behind them may be in a hurry. But i learned to embrace it - the calm italian mindset.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people are always out - there is a huge culture for going out and getting coffee our icecream or anything. its great.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Prioritize fun things with your friends - school is not as important as you think, you will surely pass the exam anyway
2) pizzaria due torri has the best slices in town - the margherita is only 1,7 euros
3) Clurricane night on tuesdays - you will meet a lot of students there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try and find housing inside the walls, preferably in the east of bologna, and even better in the south east.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends i made and all the fun we had.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Studying for the exams, not knowing if my effort was good enough.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Bologna is a really great destination! The fact that the city is walkable makes is really perfect for students.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
